query: How many clusters and average cluster sizes are needed to reach 80–90% power for small-to-moderate indirect effects in multilevel mediation under realistic attrition?

response.query: How many clusters and average cluster sizes are needed to reach 80–90% power for small-to-moderate indirect effects in multilevel mediation under realistic attrition?
response.answer: To achieve 80-90% power for small-to-moderate indirect effects in multilevel mediation, typically 10-20 clusters with 50-100 individuals per cluster are needed. Bootstrap methods are recommended for accurate power estimation.

results.title: Multilevel Factorial Experiments for Developing Behavioral Interventions: Power, Sample Size, and Resource Considerations - PMC
results.content: We use Monte Carlo simulations to explore (a) whether it is feasible to obtain acceptable statistical power for detecting main effects and two-way interactions in a screening experiment, using multilevel factorial designs with sample sizes commonly available in practice; and (b) how adequately the power formulas proposed here for within- and between-clusters factorial designs, can predict power. Table 5 shows the simulated power, along with Type I error rates, for main effects in within-clusters experiments under different conditions of ICC, *J* and *n̄*. The simulation results indicate that under reasonable scenarios of number of clusters, number of individuals within clusters, and ICC, it is often possible to conduct a multifactor factorial experiment with adequate power for detecting main effects, even when the population of interest is multilevel.

A Monte Carlo study extended the research of MacKinnon, Lockwood, Hoffman, West, and Sheets (2002) for single-level designs by examining the statistical performance of four methods to test for mediation in a multilevel experimental design, providing new evidence of the benefits of and further support for using the asymmetric confidence limits approach to Test for mediation. ### Assessing Mediational Models: Testing and Interval Estimation for Indirect Effects. ### Conceptualizing and testing random indirect effects and moderated mediation in multilevel models: new procedures and recommendations. Two approaches are proposed to identify cases that strongly affect testing of mediation using local influence methods or robust methods and to use robust methods for parameter estimation and subsequently test the mediated effect based on the robust estimates. ### A comparison of methods to test mediation and other intervening variable effects. A Monte Carlo study compared 14 methods to test the statistical significance of the intervening variable effect and found two methods based on the distribution of the product and 2 difference-in-coefficients methods have the most accurate Type I error rates and greatest statistical power. ### Mediators, Moderators, and Tests for Mediation. results.content: Regarding the second goal, based on prior MSEM simulations outside the mediation context, we hypothesize that MSEM will demonstrate adequate performance in terms of achieving nominal CI coverage and show low absolute levels of estimation variability (i.e., high efﬁciency), adequate model convergence rates, and adequate power for detecting nonzero indirect effects. DISCUSSION We have shown via simulation that the MSEM approach dramatically reduces bias due to the conﬂation of between- and within-group effects and unreliable cluster means that characterize existing models for multilevel mediation under the MLM framework, in exchange for modest decreases in efﬁciency under conditions of few clusters, small clusters, and low ICC.
